Article Title: 'FriYAY plans? We got ideas for you!' CJP issues call for Tiranga march at 5pm as CP park shut
Article Text:
CJP calls for a 5pm ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place

'Ready to go to jail for waving Tiranga': Dipke

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Friday called on its supporters and the general public to gather at Central Park in Connaught Place at 5pm for its ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march, even as the park has been shut to the public for two days on administrative grounds.The New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) announced that Central Park would remain closed on Friday and Saturday. Delhi Police, meanwhile, said it could facilitate a select group of people to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable location.The CJP announced the march amid its ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. The outfit has been demanding his removal.In a social media post announcing the march, the CJP used the tagline, “FriYAY plans? We got ideas for you!”CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said late Thursday night that he feared Delhi Police could detain him ahead of the proposed march, alleging that investigators were keeping him under watch at his residence.Addressing a press conference, Dipke said the outfit would peacefully go to Central Park to wave the national flag.“Tomorrow, we will peacefully go (to Central Park) and wave the Tiranga. As the citizens of this country, if you consider this to be a crime, then you are the biggest traitor,” he said.“If we have to go to jail for waving the tricolour, we are ready for it,” he added.Questioning the decision to close Central Park, Dipke asked whether authorities would shut down multiple locations if the group decided to wave the national flag at several places. He also questioned whether a political rally would be cancelled if people waved the Tricolour there.Dipke alleged that vehicles without number plates were following him and that Intelligence Bureau personnel were seeking updates from the watchman outside his house. He said he would not be intimidated by the possibility of detention.The CJP founder also cited the judicial custody of party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were detained after entering Jantar Mantar while waving the national flag on October 13.The outfit has accused the government of restricting peaceful protest and demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar, while Dipke said the demand was not for a change of government but for the appointment of a new election commissioner through an independent and impartial process.Calling the situation an “Emergency”, Dipke alleged that the government was acting against those questioning the Election Commission. These were his allegations; the authorities’ stated position is that the park closure is for administrative reasons.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Friday called on its supporters and the general public to gather at Central Park in Connaught Place at 5pm. The park has been shut to the public for two days on administrative grounds. Delhi Police said it could facilitate a select group of people to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable location.

Article Title: 'Hope better sense prevails': SC flags traders' livelihood concerns as Delhi braces for CJP's Tiranga march
Article Text:
SC declines urgent plea against Central Park closure ahead of ’s Tiranga march

CJP says protest will go ahead

Security tightened ahead of ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ march

Police cite law and order concerns

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined an urgent hearing on a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to shut Central Park in Connaught Place ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra do Tiranga’ protest, saying it hoped “better sense will prevail” among all concerned.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was conscious of the difficulties that a closure could cause to small shopkeepers and their families, while observing that the right to protest, the need to maintain law and order and the livelihood of traders were interconnected issues.“We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship and difficulty entire families will face,” the bench said.Justice Bagchi said the court could intervene if the restrictions resulted in business losses, adding that it would consider exercising its constitutional jurisdiction if required."If there's loss of business, we will exercise our powers under Constitutional jurisdiction. Let's cross that bridge when it comes," Justice Bagchi said.During the hearing, the petitioner's lawyer submitted that the NDMC had issued directions late Thursday night to close Central Park, effectively preventing businesses from operating in the area. The civic body had announced that the park would remain closed to the public on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons.The bench indicated that the plea could be listed on October 26 or 27.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on citizens to gather at Central Park with the national flag at 5 pm on Friday, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park and security restrictions.In a post on X, Dipke defended the party's protests, rejected allegations that it was promoting anarchy and accused the government of restricting democratic rights."Businesses do not suffer because of peaceful protests. They suffer when the govt decides to shut down an entire city, suspend internet services and restrict the movement of its own citizens and turn the city into a war-zone.""Since its inception, the Cockroach Janta Party has maintained that we will always follow Mahatma Gandhi’s path of peace and non-violence, and we have stood by that commitment. We have organised protests in Mumbai, Pune, Jaipur, Lucknow, Bengaluru and Nagpur, and every single one of them has been peaceful. I was personally assaulted in Jaipur, but even then, I chose not to retaliate because responding to violence with violence goes against everything we believe in. We would rather exercise the rights guaranteed to us by the Constitution, drafted under the leadership of Dr. BR Ambedkar, than resort to physical force. Our strength comes from our commitment to constitutional values, and no amount of provocation will make us abandon them.""Despite this, there are constant attempts to portray us as anarchists simply because we refuse to remain silent. But demanding answers from the govt is not anarchy, protesting against injustice on the streets is not anarchy, and questioning those who hold public office is certainly not anarchy. These are the most fundamental expressions of democracy. The very party that is in power today spent decades organising protests, taking to the streets and questioning the governments of the day when it was in opposition. Had the same restrictions, intimidation and police crackdowns been used against them, many of those who occupy positions of power today might never have reached where they are. It is deeply hypocritical to celebrate protests as a democratic right when you are in opposition and treat the same act as a threat to public order when you come to power.""We are not asking for privileges or special treatment. We are simply asking to exercise the rights that belong to every citizen of this Republic, irrespective of which party is in power. So let us fulfil our duty as citizens of this country by questioning those we elect, demanding accountability and speaking up whenever we witness injustice.""A govt that has been elected by the people is bound to listen to the people, not silence them. Democracy does not end once the votes have been counted."The proposed demonstration comes amid a standoff between the CJP and Delhi Police over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The CJP had announced the march after Das and Ranka were arrested for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation. They were subsequently remanded to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail.Dipke has urged political parties and civil society organisations to set aside ideological differences and join the demonstration."I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved," Dipke said at a press conference on Thursday.He also questioned the scale of voter deletions during the SIR exercise and alleged that the revisions could affect electoral outcomes."The margin of victory in 2024 was just 2 per cent. Over 13 crore voters deleted -- around 14 percent," he said."Where 2 per cent is deciding the election, you are deleting 13 crore votes. What is this if not a setting?" he added.The CJP has alleged that the government is shielding Kumar from scrutiny. These allegations have not been established by the court.Delhi Police has said Connaught Place is not a designated site for protests and that demonstrations can be held at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permissions."Jantar Mantar has been denotified as a designated protest site. Protesters can hold demonstrations at Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after obtaining the requisite permission," a senior police officer said.Security has been tightened around Connaught Place and Jantar Mantar, with several companies of paramilitary personnel stationed in the national capital. Police are deploying personnel at strategic locations, erecting barricades and regulating the movement of protesters and commuters to prevent any untoward incident.The NDMC issued its closure notice on Thursday, stating that Central Park would remain shut on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons. The decision came a day after the CJP announced its proposed march at the park, located in the centre of Connaught Place's inner circle.The party's agitation began in Mumbai on October 2 and subsequently moved to Delhi. On October 10, a planned demonstration at Jantar Mantar was met with a police crackdown, with Dipke, Das and Ranka detained at the airport after arriving from Mumbai. Opposition leaders, activists and students were also detained during protests in the capital.On October 13, CJP members entered the barricaded Jantar Mantar site carrying the national flag and were detained.Opposition parties and student organisations have separately held demonstrations against the SIR exercise and demanded accountability from the Election Commission. INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission headquarters on October 6 and were stopped by police barricades. Opposition leaders later met President Droupadi Murmu on October 9 to raise their concerns.The CJP has since framed its proposed Connaught Place march as a campaign for voting rights and the constitutional right to protest, setting up another confrontation over the restrictions imposed on demonstrations in central Delhi.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court declined an urgent hearing on a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council's decision to shut Central Park in Connaught Place. The bench said it hoped “better sense will prevail” among all concerned. The party has said it will proceed with the march despite the closure of the park and security restrictions.

Article Title: 'Bangladesh-style regime change' bid: Rajnath slams opposition over Delhi protests
Article Text:
'Conspiracy to seize power by anarchy': Rajnath Singh slams Congress protest against EC, says party seeks 'regime change'

Rajnath Singh targets Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday accused the Congress and its allies of attempting to destabilise India through protests against the Election Commission , alleging that their objective was to bring about a Bangladesh-style regime change by creating political unrest.Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Singh said opposition parties were using young people as instruments of political confrontation and attempting to create chaos under the pretext of electoral reforms and the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise."Attempts are being made to use the nation's youth as pawns in a politics of chaos. Some seek a regime change—modelled after the events in Bangladesh—openly admitting that they drew inspiration from the situation in Bangladesh; others, meanwhile, brazenly call for the toppling of the government. This makes it clear that their sole agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country ablaze...their struggle is not for electoral reform, nor is it about SIR or Gyanesh Kumar; it is not for the sake of a bright future for the nation's youth—rather, it is a conspiracy to seize power by inciting anarchy in the country. .."The defence minister's remarks come amid continuing protests by opposition parties, INDIA bloc leaders and student organisations against the Election Commission's electoral roll revision exercise and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Singh also targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of undermining constitutional institutions and using allegations of electoral irregularities for political gains."India's constitutional bodies cannot be made sacrificial for political interests. This needs to be understood. Through false outrage, attempts to malign institutions and political opportunism, India's development journey cannot be affected. Instead of indulging in politics of disruption, Rahul Gandhi should respect the public mandate and do self-introspection of his political role."The defence minister further questioned Gandhi's allegations concerning voter lists, citing claims involving alleged duplicate and fake voters."Rahul Gandhi once claimed that a 70-year-old woman was a double voter. On another occasion, he alleged that a 35-year-old woman was a 124-year-old voter. At times, he even attempted to defame ordinary citizens by labelling them as fake voters...his own party never filed a single formal appeal regarding the electoral rolls; the reason being that they had absolutely no evidence to support such claims. We have never cast doubt upon constitutional institutions—that is simply our character. We have never questioned the nation’s electoral system, nor have we ever sought to mislead the public by defaming constitutional institutions. We have always held the people of this country, the Constitution, and our constitutional institutions in high regard..."Singh maintained that the Congress had failed to substantiate its allegations against the electoral system and accused the opposition of attempting to discredit constitutional institutions.Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary also alleged that efforts were underway to destabilise the country and interfere with constitutional institutions."A conspiracy to destabilise the country is going on. An attempt to make changes to constitutional bodies is also being made..."Rajnath also took a swipe at the Congress's electoral prospects in Uttar Pradesh, pointing to its prolonged absence from power in the state and questioning Rahul Gandhi's political strength without the support of the Samajwadi Party."The Congress party has been out of power in Uttar Pradesh for 37 years...I would like to ask Rahul Gandhi: without the Samajwadi Party, do you even have the capability to win your own seat in Rae Bareli?"
Article Summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh accuses Congress of attempting to destabilise India through protests against the Election Commission. Singh says opposition parties are using young people as instruments of political confrontation and attempting to create chaos under the pretext of electoral reforms. Singh also targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of undermining constitutional institutions.

Article Title: ICMR picks 7 centres to develop priority medical devices, diagnostics
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Seven research centres across leading Indian institutions have been selected by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to develop priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies, with projects spanning portable screening for primary healthcare, biomaterials and technologies for eye and vascular diseases.The selected institutions are the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) at Kharagpur, Delhi, Bombay, Kanpur and Madras, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Coimbatore.Among the selected projects, IIT Bombay's centre, led by Dr Abhijit Majumder, will focus on portable screening, monitoring and point-of-care medical technologies for primary healthcare. Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham's centre, led by Prof Gopal S Pillai, will work on developing, validating and translating healthcare technologies for ophthalmic and vascular diseases, while IISc Bengaluru will focus on biomaterials and translational medical devices.IIT Kharagpur's PRAGATICAR, led by Prof Suman Chakraborty, will focus on frugal diagnostics, regenerative and personalised healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital health and advanced therapeutics. IIT Delhi's CAR-PATH, led by Prof Vivekanandan Perumal, will work on priority applied technologies for healthcare.At IIT Kanpur, Prof Amitabha Bandyopadhyay will lead a multidisciplinary proposal to develop 10 priority healthcare products.IIT Madras will host TARaNGaM, a translational hub for next-generation medical technology, devices and diagnostics, led by Prof Mohanasankar Sivaprakasam.The initiative aims to accelerate the development of affordable, accessible and indigenous healthcare technologies addressing unmet clinical needs. To identify these needs, ICMR undertook an exercise involving clinicians from different healthcare settings, including tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 cities, and drew up a curated list of around 100 priority medical device and diagnostic technologies.Under the original call for proposals, applicants were required to propose the development of at least eight to 10 technologies from this list, covering a mix of low-risk and high-risk products. The scheme provides for funding of up to Rs 15 crore per centre over five years, with an emphasis on regulatory-compliant product development and eventual commercialisation.The call prioritised institutions with a track record in research, prototyping, technology transfer and commercialisation. It also required centres to leverage existing infrastructure, build a trained medical technology research workforce and continue functioning beyond the funding period, with host institutions expected to sustain them as permanent activities.The key challenge will be translating research into validated products that can address clinical needs and reach patients. The results list does not specify the individual devices to be developed by most of the selected centres, their development timelines or when the technologies could become available for clinical use.
Article Summary: Seven research centres selected by Indian Council of Medical Research to develop priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies. The selected institutions are the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) at Kharagpur, Delhi, Bombay, Kanpur and Madras. The initiative aims to accelerate the development of affordable, accessible and indigenous healthcare technologies addressing unmet clinical needs.

Article Title: Middle East conflict: India pushes for 'resolution through dialogue and diplomacy' at UNSC

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East, warning that the escalating hostilities pose a serious threat to regional stability and the safety of Indian nationals.Speaking at the UN Security Council ’s open debate on the Middle East, Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region, highlighting that around 10 million Indians live in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and contribute to their economies.He called for restraint and de-escalation, expressing concern over attacks on civilian infrastructure that have resulted in casualties, including the death of Indian citizen Mohammed Yusuf Ali in Riyadh.Harish said India stood in complete solidarity with the government and people of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty following the recent attacks.He also raised concerns over attacks on commercial shipping, including the India-flagged MV DP World Kaveri earlier this week and MT Petro Dolphin and MT Walthera last week.“All attacks on commercial shipping and merchant mariners are legally and morally indefensible,” he said, adding that several of the affected vessels had Indian seafarers whose safety and security remained India's direct responsibility.India reiterated the need for an immediate de-escalation of hostilities and a resolution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.Harish said attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease, stressing that freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways must be upheld in accordance with international law.He further added that focus on maritime security must not divert attention from the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. It condemned the October 7, 2023 attacks and reiterated its support for a negotiated two-state solution, the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2803, and continued development and humanitarian assistance.v
Article Summary: India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Parvathaneni Harish, on Friday condemned attacks on commercial vessels and civilian infrastructure in the Middle East. Harish said India had “very high stakes” in the safety, security and stability of the region.

Article Title: If every citizen becomes a journalist, it will create problems for all, says SC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. “We must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,” he said. Justice Bagchi said, “It will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.CJI Kant said, “The issue requires detailed examination — whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.” Justice Bagchi added, “The Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.”Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.
Article Summary: PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues. Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists.

Article Title: Violent Naxalism isover, task now is toheal wounds: Amit Shah
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah Thursday said not just Left-wing extremism but every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.Addressing the event via video conferencing, Shah said the programme, organised under 'seva sankalp abhiyan' to mark 25 years of PM Modi's 'seva and samarpan' (service), would help tribal people who had lost limbs or sensory abilities due to Naxal violence. Chhattisgarh govt organised it with welfare organisations such as Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahayata Samiti and Bharatiya Jain Sanghatana to provide prosthetic devices, wheelchairs, crutches and hearing aids.Held in Jagdalpur from Oct 5 to 7, the campaign benefited over 3,600 persons with disabilities, including over 1,570 from Bastar. Shah said Maoists' use of IEDs to maim innocent civilians for political objectives was a grave human rights violation.Though violent Naxalism was eliminated by the March 31, 2026 deadline, Shah said, the task would remain unfinished until govt healed victims' wounds, helped them stand and ensured they lived with dignity.Bastar was becoming vibrant again, he said, citing participation in Bastar Olympics and Bastar Pandum. Shah said 8,526 Naxalites had surrendered. Accounts had been opened for 7,328, reward money given to 1,620, incentives provided to 7,882, jobs offered to 455 and land allotted to 129. Another 4,014 beneficiaries had received houses under PM Awas Yojana, while over 2,308 tribal people had undergone skill training.A total of 6,763 ration cards had been issued, 2,808 families provided free electricity and work begun on 372 road projects. 48,526 people had received Aadhaar cards and 44 gram panchayats were recognised under 'Ilwad Panchayat Awards'.Twenty of the 50 security camps in Chhattisgarh will be converted into Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera, providing public services, skill training and PDS benefits to nearby villages, Shah said. "The places where our security forces once sat to protect you will become the places where officials will lay the foundation for a developed Bastar," Shah added. tnn
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah said every trace of misery caused by five decades of Maoist violence must be wiped out. At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.

NEW DELHI: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal on Thursday launched the Jan Neeti Bharat party and announced that it would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career to pursue politics independently.In a video message on X, Mittal said the party will focus on making people central to policymaking and ensuring that the government remains accountable to them throughout its five-year term, rather than only on election day."Politics rules over you. In Jan Neeti, you will be the ones who rule," she said, announcing the party's name and its decision to contest the state polls due early next year.Her decision to launch a party of her own places her among a group of civil servants who left government service before their scheduled retirement to enter politics.Here are 10 former civil servants who made the transition from bureaucracy to politics before completing their service.Yashwant Sinha resigned from the Indian Administrative Service in 1984 to enter active politics. He joined the Janata Party and subsequently became associated with the Janata Dal before joining the BJP.Sinha first served as Union finance minister in the Chandra Shekhar government in 1990-91.Under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he returned to the finance ministry in 1998 and held the portfolio until 2002, when he became external affairs minister.His political career also included membership of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Sinha later distanced himself from the BJP and joined the Trinamool Congress in 2021, before contesting the 2022 presidential election as the opposition's joint candidate.Ajit Jogi left the IAS in 1986 to enter politics and joined the Congress. He had served as a district collector before moving into political life and was subsequently elected to the Rajya Sabha.Jogi's biggest political breakthrough came in 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh. He became the newly created state's first chief minister, holding office until 2003.After years in the Congress, Jogi broke away from the party in 2016 and founded the Janata Congress Chhattisgarh, seeking to establish an independent regional political platform.His career stands out as an example of a former administrator moving from district-level governance to the leadership of a newly formed state and later attempting to build a party of his own.Mani Shankar Aiyar resigned from the Indian Foreign Service in 1989 to enter politics. He had served as a diplomat for more than two decades and spent part of his career on deputation to the Prime Minister's Office under Rajiv Gandhi.Aiyar joined the Congress and won the Mayiladuthurai Lok Sabha seat in Tamil Nadu in 1991. He went on to become a prominent party leader and served as Union minister for petroleum and natural gas during the UPA government.He also held the panchayati raj portfolio and was involved in efforts to strengthen local self-government institutions.Arvind Kejriwal resigned from the Indian Revenue Service in 2006 after working in the income tax department. He had become involved in the Right to Information movement and founded the non-governmental organisation Parivartan to address citizens' grievances.His political journey gathered momentum during the Ana Hazare-led India Against Corruption movement, which campaigned for a stronger anti-corruption law. In 2012, Kejriwal founded the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), choosing to build a political organisation rather than join an established party.AAP made its electoral debut in the 2013 Delhi assembly elections, when Kejriwal defeated then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He became Delhi chief minister in December 2013 and returned to the post after the party's victories in 2015 and 2020.KJ Alphons took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2006 and entered electoral politics in Kerala. He contested the Kanjirappally assembly seat in Kerala as an independent candidate supported by the Left Democratic Front and won.Alphons later founded the Jana Shakti platform before joining the BJP in 2011. His political journey subsequently took him to Parliament, when he became a Rajya Sabha member.In 2017, he was inducted into the Narendra Modi government as Union minister of state for tourism, with independent charge, and also handled electronics and information technology.His transition from a civil servant known for urban development initiatives to a state-level politician and Union minister is an example of an officer moving across political formations during his career.Satyapal Singh, a 1980-batch IPS officer of the Maharashtra cadre, opted for voluntary retirement in January 2014 while serving as Mumbai police commissioner, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections.He joined the BJP and contested the Baghpat Lok Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2014, defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Ajit Singh. He retained the constituency in the 2019 general election.Singh served as Union minister of state for human resource development and water resources during the Modi government's first term. Before entering politics, he had served in several police leadership roles and was known for his work in law enforcement.OP Choudhary, a 2005-batch IAS officer, resigned from the service in 2018 while serving as Raipur collector to enter politics. He joined the BJP and contested the Kharsia assembly constituency in Chhattisgarh in the same year.Choudhary lost that election but returned to the electoral contest in 2023, this time winning the Raipur City South seat. He was subsequently inducted into the Chhattisgarh government as a minister.His career highlights the uncertain transition from administration to politics. Unlike officers who win their first election, Choudhary's initial defeat did not end his political ambitions. He returned five years later and secured a place in the state Cabinet.Aparajita Sarangi, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, took voluntary retirement in 2018 while serving as joint secretary in the Union rural development ministry.She joined the BJP in November that year and contested the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Bhubaneswar. Sarangi won the seat, defeating Biju Janata Dal candidate Arup Patnaik.She retained the constituency in the 2024 general election, establishing herself as a BJP leader in Odisha.Sarangi's transition was particularly swift: she moved from a senior central government position to an electoral contest within months of leaving the service and subsequently secured two consecutive Lok Sabha victories.AK Sharma, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Gujarat cadre, took voluntary retirement in January 2021, around 18 months before his scheduled superannuation.Sharma had spent a substantial part of his career working in the Prime Minister's Office and was associated with Narendra Modi's administration during his tenure as Gujarat chief minister and later as prime minister.After leaving the service, Sharma joined the BJP and was elected to the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council. He subsequently became a minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, handling portfolios including urban development and energy.His move demonstrated how a senior bureaucrat with experience in the central administration could enter state politics and secure a position in the Cabinet without first contesting a direct assembly election.Asim Arun, a 1994-batch IPS officer, took voluntary retirement in January 2022 while serving as Kanpur police commissioner. He joined the BJP soon afterwards, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Arun contested the Kannauj assembly seat and won, entering a constituency associated with the Samajwadi Party. He was subsequently inducted into the Yogi Adityanath government.His political entry came within weeks of his voluntary retirement, making him one of the clearest recent examples of a serving police officer moving directly into electoral politics before the end of his career.K Annamalai, a 2011-batch IPS officer of the Karnataka cadre, resigned from the police service in September 2019, before completing his tenure. He had served as superintendent of police in Udupi and Chikkamagaluru districts before leaving the force.He joined the BJP in August 2020 and rose rapidly through the party's ranks. In July 2021, he was appointed the BJP's Tamil Nadu president, becoming one of the party's most prominent faces in the state.Annamalai contested the 2021 Tamil Nadu assembly election from Aravakurichi but lost to the DMK's R Elango. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, he contested from Coimbatore but lost to DMK candidate Ganapathi P Rajkumar.In June 2026, Annamalai quit the BJP following differences with the party leadership over its political strategy in Tamil Nadu and launched a new political movement, 'We The Leaders'. He said the movement would focus on "common man politics", challenge what he described as "cult and dynastic politics", and eventually evolve into a political party. He has outlined plans to contest the 2031 Tamil Nadu assembly elections.
Article Summary: Divya Mittal launched her party, the Jan Neeti Bharat Party, on Thursday. The party will contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Her announcement comes nearly a month after she took voluntary retirement from the civil services, ending a 13-year administrative career.

NEW DELHI: India’s Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday strongly pushed back against Indian-origin Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal 's social media post on the country's democratic framework and electoral procedures, calling it an "interference" in India's internal affairs."The remarks by @RepJayapal on India’s electoral and political processes are unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs," he posted on X.Emphasising India’s longstanding record of conducting free and fair elections, Kwatra invited Jayapal for a “constructive conversation” to address her concerns."India is a vibrant democracy, with robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections. Always open to constructive conversation with the Congresswoman to dispel her misconceptions," he added.Kwatra's response came after Jayapal alleged a sweeping removal of citizens from India's draft electoral list."I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls. This appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing here at home to undermine voting rights in a democracy," the Congresswoman said."Protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections. Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India," she wrote in a follow-up post.Her remarks came amid the ongoing protests in India against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls exercise.According to data released by the Election Commission (EC), approximately 72 million entries were removed from draft electoral rolls across 13 states and Union territories during the initial two phases of the SIR.Furthermore, during the ongoing third phase, which encompasses the publication of draft lists across 18 states and UTs, the number of excluded electors totals 61.6 million.Addressing these omissions, the EC clarified that if a legitimate elector's name was accidentally omitted during the SIR process, the individual retains the right to apply for reinstatement through the claims and objections mechanism, followed by the submission of Form 6.

Article Title: NHAI warning prompts IGI T3 parking operator to lift FASTag curbs
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The parking operator at Terminal 3 (T3) of Delhi airport has removed FASTag -based entry restrictions, bringing much-needed relief to passengers and visitors. The move came a day after Indian Highways Management Company Ltd (IHMCL), under NHAI, warned the acquiring bank associated with the parking facility of action after it emerged that the operator was using FASTag to regulate vehicle entry rather than solely for collecting parking fees.NHAI had also temporarily suspended FASTag-based parking payments, citing the violation.In a post on X, NHAI said, “NHAI would like to inform you that the matter was taken up with the relevant stakeholders to address the inconvenience faced by commuters. The parking operator had recently started diverting vehicles without FASTag to the multi-level parking facility, causing inconvenience to users. Vehicles entering this facility often get stuck in queues, exceeding the free parking period and forcing motorists to pay parking fees.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) on Thursday filed a criminal contempt petition against journalist Nikhil Wagle and Uddhav Sena leader Sanjay Raut over their disparaging remarks against Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant.Attorney General R Venkataramani has since granted consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against the two under the Contempt of Courts Act.The statements came after Chief Justice of India (CJI) declined a request last week from a delegation of opposition parties to meet him in person. The CJI said the delegation could instead file a petition before the court.According to the petition, Wagle subsequently posted "**** you CJI!" on his X account in response to a report about the CJI's decision. However, Wagle later deleted his tweet and posted an apology.Raut's remarks to the media were carried by news agency IANS on X on October 12."We have also seen judges attending political programs of the BJP in states where it is in power, and chief ministers organizing dinners to welcome high court and Supreme Court judges," Raut was quoted as saying. The petition further states that he referred to photographs purportedly showing judges playing badminton with political figures in London."The aforementioned statement is false and contrary to records and is made to scandalise and diminish the authority of the Hon'ble Supreme Court," the petition states.The petition cites a June 19 order of the Delhi high court , which found that photographs circulated as being from a badminton event in London were actually from an event held at Thyagaraj Stadium in New Delhi in November 2025. The High Court had directed that the content be taken down.The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) clarified that it did not seek to prevent fair and temperate criticism of the judiciary, reported Bar and Bench.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) filed a criminal contempt petition against journalist Nikhil Wagle and Uddhav Sena leader Sanjay Raut. Wagle posted "**** you CJI!" on his X account in response to a report about the CJI's decision. Raut's remarks were carried by news agency IANS on X on October 12.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place on Friday, Delhi Police said it may consider allowing a select group of people to gather at a suitable location to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem. The statement comes amid restrictions on gatherings in the area and the New Delhi Municipal Council’s (NDMC) decision to shut Central Park for two days.DCP PRO Neha Yadav said the CJP had appealed to the public through social media and a press conference to assemble at Central Park at 5 pm on October 16. She added that the Aam Aadmi Party had also urged its workers, supporters and the general public to attend in large numbers.“Given the current security and law-and-order situation, a prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is already in effect in Connaught Place and its surrounding areas, aimed at maintaining peace and order and ensuring the safety of individuals as well as public and private property,” Yadav said.She said Delhi Police had been asked to make security arrangements at Central Park and prevent unauthorised entry.Yadav also said market and trade associations had sought protection for their establishments, alleging that unlawful gatherings were affecting business during the festive season.“The Delhi Police appeals to protesters and the general public not to participate in any gathering that violates the orders issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which is currently in force. Appropriate legal action will be taken against those who violate these orders,” she said.Yadav added that any permitted gathering must follow the prescribed rules for the national flag and anthem. “When carrying or accompanying the national flag, and during the singing of the national anthem, prescribed rules must be followed, and the utmost respect, dignity, and decorum must be maintained toward both the tricolour and the national anthem,” she said.Earlier, in a notice dated October 15, the NDMC said, “It is hereby informed that the Central Park, Connaught Place, shall remain closed to the general public on 16th October 2026 & 17th October 2026, due to administrative reasons.”The closure comes after the CJP announced the march on Wednesday. On Thursday, founder Abhijit Dipke urged political parties and civil society groups to join the protest, saying, “I request all political parties and civil society groups to rise above ideology and come together. If the right to vote is not saved, democracy will not be saved.”Earlier, the Delhi Police told the high court that it will take “appropriate steps” against Dipke’s proposed protest.Police also cited prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), imposed to maintain law and order and protect public and private property.The submission came as the high court heard a plea by Palika Bazar vendor Anil Kumar Gupta, who sought intervention against the proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march, arguing that protests could disrupt business and threaten traders’ livelihoods.The plea was mentioned before acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre on Thursday. Senior advocate Sacchin Puri, appearing for the petitioner, told the court, “This protest has to be stopped.”The march follows the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after raising slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation at Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place on Friday. Delhi Police may allow small gathering to wave tricolour, sing anthem at CJP march.NDMC shuts Central Park on October 16-17 for 'administrative reasons'

Article Title: EC announces Special Summary Revision of voters' list in 17 states amid SIR row
Article Text:
The EC's notice comes amid the SIR row.

Notice by EC

ECI's notice to states.

How's Special Revision different from SIR

NEW DELHI: The El ec tion Commission (EC) has informed the states that it would be conducting a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states, including the poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa.In a letter to the chief electoral officers of the states and Union territories concerned, including Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa, the Election Commission said January 1, 2027, would be the qualifying date for the exercise.The Special Summary Revision (SSR) is intended to add eligible voters, especially young people and first-time electors, rectify errors in existing entries and ensure electoral rolls are accurate and up to date.The current term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly ends on May 22 next year. The tenures of the assemblies in Manipur, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand, which have 60, 40, 117 and 70 seats, respectively, are due to end on different dates in March 2027.Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Election Commission is permitted to conduct elections "earlier than six months before the term expires".While a Summary Revision focuses on new eligibles and routine corrections, SIR goes far deeper, involving statewide house-to-house verification, detailed scrutiny of entries, and large-scale data audits.For instance, under a Summary Revision, a voter who has shifted homes must file a form to update their address. Under SIR, the Booth Level Officer visits that address, confirms whether the voter still lives there, checks if anyone new has become eligible, and updates the roll based on physical verification rather than waiting for the voter to initiate the change.The SIR of electoral rolls has triggered a political controversy, with opposition parties raising concerns over the deletion of voters' names and the possibility of eligible citizens being left out of electoral lists.The poll panel has maintained that the exercise is aimed at cleaning up electoral rolls by removing duplicate and ineligible entries, including those belonging to deceased voters, while ensuring that all eligible citizens are included.ALSO READ: ‘Anarchic, immature’: BJP targets Rahul over anti-CEC protests; claims misconduct with women cop However, opposition parties have questioned the process, alleging that the exercise could lead to genuine voters losing their right to vote. They have also raised concerns over documentation requirements, verification procedures and the possibility of disproportionate effects on vulnerable groups, including migrant workers, the elderly and economically disadvantaged people.One of the main concerns surrounding SIR is the potential deletion of eligible voters' names during the verification process.The dispute has also reached the Supreme Court , with petitions raising concerns about the manner in which the revision is being conducted. The legal debate centres on the Election Commission's authority to revise electoral rolls and the safeguards available to voters who challenge their exclusion.
Article Summary: The Election Commission (EC) has informed the states that it would be conducting a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states. The states are Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa. The current term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly ends on May 22 next year.

Article Title: India to Starlink: Comply with rules before entering market
Article Text:

Mittal: Ahead of Musk in queue for approval

NEW DELHI: Starlink is yet to receive clearance to launch services in India as it has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said Wednesday, sending a tough message to tech trillionaire Elon Musk that in order to do business in India he will have to abide by the law of the land.Govt has no objection to the satellite internet provider rolling out its services once it addresses security concerns and agrees to establish local base stations before it can offer services in India, sources said. A base station is a radio transmitter and receiver that acts as a local hub, or the "first hop", connecting end-user devices to a wireless network. The requirement to set up "base stations" will help authorities to secure compliance with laws.Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Musk's Starlink are the three entities planning to start satellite communication services in India.Significantly, another message to Musk that he cannot expect to be an exception to the law came from Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal, who said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb satellite service might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue, having applied nearly five years ago.He added that he will be "very happy" to get it at least a few days before Starlink.Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Bharti Mittal on Tuesday said his company deserved to get approval to start a satellite internet service before Elon Musk’s Starlink as Airtel’s Eutelsat OneWeb had submitted its application earlier.“I am significantly ahead in the queue from him. I applied five years back. I have my ground networks ready for three years. My satellites have been hovering over India for last five years... We will be happy to get it at least a few days before him,” said Mittal at Bloomberg New Economy Forum, in response to a query soliciting his views on Musk’s recent tirade, as he accused Indian telecom providers of preventing Starlink from entering the Indian market.Govt has denied Musk’s charge that Starlink was being discriminated against at the instance of a “local oligarch”.
Article Summary: Starlink has not agreed to comply with regulations requiring satellite internet providers to set up domestic infrastructure, a senior govt official said. Bharti Enterprises chairperson Sunil Mittal said Airtel's Eutelsat OneWeb might receive regulatory approvals ahead of Starlink, as it is "way ahead" in the approval queue.

Article Title: Stent safety concerns reach Centre after reports of complications with Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade has urged a review of coronary stent safety standards after reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet Secretariat has taken up concerns over the safety and quality of coronary stents with the Union health ministry after a Rajya Sabha MP sought intervention following reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka.In an October 5 letter, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan acknowledged a representation from Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade, a medical doctor, said it had been forwarded to the department of health and family welfare for appropriate action and a reply.Gopchade’s September 28 representation cited media reports that Sri Lanka’s regulator had directed the withdrawal of three models of Indian-manufactured drug-eluting stents over concerns including improper positioning, stent dislodgement, acute stent thrombosis and failure to expand properly. The reported issues were identified during an investigation by Sri Lanka’s Medical Device Evaluation Committee, according to the letter.The MP cautioned that the reported concerns might not all ultimately be substantiated, but said they warranted scrutiny of existing safeguards for device performance, clinical appropriateness and the detection of complications after implantation.The representation calls for more stringent pre-market testing of stents and delivery systems, including assessments of durability, deployment, expansion and dislodgement.It also seeks stronger clinical documentation to ensure stenting is performed only when medically indicated and alternatives are considered where appropriate.A key recommendation is end-to-end traceability through batch and serial numbers for every implanted stent, allowing affected devices and patients to be identified quickly if a safety alert emerges. The MP has also sought stronger adverse-event reporting, particularly for stent thrombosis, migration, incomplete expansion, deformation and delivery-system complications.The representation further calls for a mechanism to swiftly review safety alerts, recalls and withdrawals issued by foreign regulators when the same or similar devices are marketed in India. Better patient follow-up and long-term safety data collection have also been proposed to detect emerging risks early.Citing regulatory guidance from the US, the UK and Canada, Gopchade highlighted the importance of engineering and durability testing, clinical evidence, traceability and timely regulatory action when safety signals emerge. He urged the health ministry and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) to examine the issues with cardiology experts and other stakeholders.The Cabinet Secretariat’s communication does not establish that the government has accepted the allegations, ordered a formal investigation or approved new regulatory measures. The reported concerns also do not, by themselves, establish that similar complications have occurred in India.
Article Summary: Cabinet Secretariat has taken up concerns over the safety and quality of coronary stents with the Union health ministry. Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Madhavrao Gopchade has sought intervention following reports of complications involving Indian-made devices in Sri Lanka.

NEW DELHI: A 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy will be burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations in the national capital this year, with organisers saying the insect will symbolise filth and unhygienic conditions as part of their cleanliness message.The Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee, which organises the Ramlila in Pitampura, said the initiative aims to highlight the need to eliminate filth from homes, neighbourhoods and society at large, in keeping with the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.Ashok Goel Devaraha, president of the committee and Model Town BJP MLA, said the decision was intended to reinforce the message of the triumph of good over evil and was not politically motivated.Speaking to ANI, Devaraha said Vijayadashami symbolises the victory of truth over falsehood and righteousness over unrighteousness. He added that the committee had previously burnt effigies representing issues affecting the country, including Naxalism and terrorism.“Keeping these principles in mind, we have also, in the past, burned effigies representing various afflictions plaguing our nation, such as Naxalism or terrorism.This year, our committee has decided to burn an effigy of a cockroach, a symbol of filth,” he said.The effigy will be set alight at the committee grounds in Pitampura. Devaraha described it as a 30-foot-tall structure shaped like a cockroach, adding that the aim was to draw attention to the need to rid homes, neighbourhoods and society of dirt and unhygienic conditions.The choice of the insect comes amid protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition parties in Delhi, which had been campaigning against former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and is now demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The group staged protests against Pradhan in June and July, including a demonstration at Jantar Mantar and a march towards Parliament on July 20. Pradhan subsequently resigned as education minister in July, while Pralhad Joshi took over the portfolio.The CJP has since returned to the streets over its allegations concerning the electoral roll revision process, joining opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations. Several activists, students and journalists were detained during protests in the capital.The committee president, however, has denied that the cockroach effigy is politically motivated, maintaining that it is intended to convey a message about cleanliness.Also read: 6,000 cops, 200 CAPF companies: As CJP pushes ahead with Tiranga march, Delhi prepares for a high-security friday On May 15, while hearing a case in the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant had compared certain individuals with fraudulent degrees to “cockroaches” who become social media or RTI activists to attack the system. The remarks triggered widespread backlash among young people and inspired the satirical “Cockroach Janta Party” (CJP) movement.He later clarified that his oral remarks during a Supreme Court hearing were “misquoted” and later used with “malicious intent” to mislead the country’s youth.
Article Summary: 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy will be burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations. Organisers say insect will symbolise filth and unhygienic conditions as part of cleanliness message.

Article Title: ‘Suspension of cellular internet services needed in exigencies’: MHA reply to SC notice
Article Text:
Mobile internet has to be curbed in exigencies MHA reply to SC notice

NEW DELHI: Continuing with its tough stand against protesters, the home ministry Thursday sought modification of Supreme Court ’s Oct 11 order for allowing “unhindered internet services” and said exigencies such as disturbance of public order required temporary suspension of cellular internet services, as was the case between 10 pm on Oct 9 to 10 pm on Oct 10 in a 4-km radius of Raisina Hill.In an affidavit filed in response to a contempt of court notice, home secretary Govind Mohan justified Delhi Police ’s request for suspension of cellular internet services and said it was “found to be a proportionate measure, having regard to the magnitude of the situation and the need to prevent any disturbance of public order in the national capital”.“The suspension was confined to cellular internet services and did not extend to non-cellular internet services or telecommunications services such as wi-fi and broadband,” he said, emphasising that suspension of such services was considered a recognised measure to maintain public order in appropriate circumstances.The home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and DMRC chairperson tendered unconditional apology to the court through their affidavits before going on to explain why the steps were taken to prevent unlawful gathering at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10.Though the affidavit conveyed an “unconditional apology“ to the court for the “contempt” charge, it marked a defiant assertion of the Centre’s legal competence and willingness to take strong measures to control "illegal“ protests.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the “apology” was meant to meet a procedural requirement. “The law is well settled that whenever response is filed pursuant to contempt notice, first sentence we write is that we hereby tender an unconditional apology. And thereafter, we have explained how the contempt is not made out,” he said.“It is with reference to compliance of that law that in every affidavit, this is the first paragraph. Now, in media and social media, things are going on that govt has apologised and they want to say nothing,” he complained.CJI Kant said, “We have not read those media reports, nor are we taking cognisance of any such report.” Justice Bagchi added, “We are neither taking cognisance of the media reports nor your unqualified apology. But by your submissions, it appears to be a qualified apology.”Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar said in his affidavit that permission for the CJP’s Oct 10 protest at Jantar Manor was denied due to past experience of large-scale violence during its July 20 protests, inability of organisers to control supporters and the grave inconvenience caused to general public because of a string of protests from Oct 6-8 that choked central Delhi for days together.Narrating the sensitivity of central Delhi, housing Rashtrapati Bhavan, Parliament, Supreme Court, embassies and other institutions requiring a complex security arrangement as well as measures for maintaining public order, the commissioner said, “No police administration can permit any breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent events of Oct 6, 7, 8. ”He added, “Due to all these marches, central Delhi areas got completely choked and there were huge traffic snarls for long hours, resulting in students and innocent citizens getting stuck in traffic jams, resulting in them missing their trains, airlines etc.“The gatherings were very aggressive, fuelled by persons under the cover of ‘freelance journalism’, who were physically harassing policemen, some miscreants were misbehaving with lady police personnel resulting in injuries to over a dozen police personnel.”The commissioner said in compliance with the law laid down by the SC, the police removed illegally gathered people from the site where prohibitory orders were in place but those detained punctured the tyres of buses in which they were kept and broke window shields in acts of violence.All those detained for attempting to protest in violation of prohibitory orders were released after a few hours and were kept in makeshift centres, not police lock-ups, he said. Police provided them with “hot, fresh and good meals” and were permitted to leave after the requirement of detention ceased to exist, he added.
Article Summary: The home ministry Thursday sought modification of Supreme Court ’s Oct 11 order for allowing “unhindered internet services’ The suspension was confined to cellular internet services and did not extend to non-cellular internet services or telecommunications services such as wi-fi and broadband.

Article Title: Fees for professional courses can be hiked midstream only in exceptional cases: SC
Article Text:
SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023- 27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a relief to students pursuing professional courses like engineering and medicine in private colleges who have to face a fee hike midstream, Supreme Court has held that any change in fee structure after admission can be allowed only in exceptional circumstances.While appreciating the contribution of self-financing institutions to the education sector, a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said there should be certainty regarding fees, and students must not be forced to pay more than that prescribed at the time of admission."For the overwhelming majority of households, the fee payable for a professional course constitutes a substantial part of the family's income and savings; it is not a matter of incidental expenditure. The parents make provisions for the fees... with the aspiration that their children will acquire better qualifications, secure better opportunities and build a future that may be better than their own. Many students and families also depend on educational loans to finance professional higher education," SC said, noting fees charged in professional courses are reported to be 711% higher than in general courses.The court said it was a matter of good governance for the state and its regulatory bodies to create an ecosystem in which there was certainty about the financial obligation that students and their families need to undertake to acquire professional qualifications."Adverse variations in financial commitment, and the insecurities that it may create, will impact the student and the family, and, in the long run, have an adverse effect on the quality and character of the professionals in the making. We are of the opinion that it is not difficult to formulate a scheme through which such uncertainties can be avoided," it said.SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023-27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal. The college had also imposed a new development fee.Passing an order in favour of students who had challenged the fee hike, the bench said, "The regulatory regime for fixation of fees, as contemplated in the decisions of this court, AICTE regulations, National Education Policy 2020 coupled with principles of certainty, necessitates the relevant authorities to notify fee payable for the entire course before a student takes admission... Variation is permissible only in exceptional instances such as unforeseen increase in the expenditure. "
Article Summary: SC quashed a 37% fee hike for BTech courses for the 2023-27 cohort at Dr BC Roy Engineering College in West Bengal. The college had also imposed a new development fee. Fees charged in professional courses are reported to be 711% higher than in general courses.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a Bombay high court order which quashed a decision of the Yes Bank administrator to write off additional tier 1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore in March 2020.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih said, "We see no reason to interfere with the impugned judgement. Article Title: HC bars fuel-run boats on Dal Lake, pushes for cleaner alternatives
Article Text:
Fuel boats used by the administration for emergency services, law and order, disaster management and rescue operations will be exempted from the order, the HC said.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K high court directed authorities Thursday to ensure no fuel-powered motorboats, including motorised shikaras and jet skis, operate on Srinagar’s Dal Lake in a move that would halt 166 such vessels.The HC cited growing pollution for the curbs -- which came in the middle of the tourist season -- and directed govt to explore whether fuel-powered boats could be replaced with solar-powered or battery-run alternatives.“This court is convinced that in modern times, when lake systems have become a growing concern for civilisation, steps are being taken to exclude activities which would cause pollution. It would be also important that whatever policy is framed is more reasonable while balancing tourism activities, pollution, as well as uniformity between the players involved,” a division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajesh Sekhri said.The bench made it clear that the restrictions would apply with immediate effect. “In case any motorised boat is allowed to ply, it shall be held as contempt of today’s order,” the HC said.Fuel boats used by the administration for emergency services, law and order, disaster management and rescue operations will be exempted from the order, the HC said. This came after additional advocate-general (AAG) Mohsin Qadri, appearing for govt, argued that such boats be spared.The order came on a batch of petitions by some owners of fuel-run boats who had moved the HC against the transport department’s failure to renew their licences. They argued that the delay violated their fundamental rights to life and livelihood. During the hearing, AAG Qadri conceded that pollution was a problem and called for a balance between tourism and cleanliness of the lake. Qadri also highlighted Dal’s civilisational importance for J&K.“Solar boats and electric (battery) boats could be a solution for balancing the equities between tourism and sustenance of the lake,” the bench said. CJ Bhati and Justice Sekhri directed govt to submit to consult experts and come up with a comprehensive policy on whether solarised or battery-run boats would be a solution. The case will be heard next on Oct 30.
Article Summary: J&K high court orders authorities to ensure no fuel-powered motorboats, including motorised shikaras and jet skis, operate on Srinagar’s Dal Lake. The HC cited growing pollution for the curbs, which came in the middle of the tourist season. The bench made it clear that the restrictions would apply with immediate effect.

NEW DELHI: BJP Thursday said the SC judgement holding that quota benefits cannot be claimed by converts was "historic", adding it is a "massive blow to the appeasement politics" of Congress and other opposition parties which have sought to provide reservation to Muslims on the basis of religion.While upholding the Madras HC order that a person converting to Islam can't claim reservation under backward class category solely on the basis of conversion, SC also held that a person who professes a religion other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism cannot be considered a member of Scheduled Castes (SC).BJP's Gaurav Bhatia lauded the "landmark" ruling, which is a boost to the party's long-held position that Muslims and Christians cannot claim rights accorded to Dalits because of their SC family background and that OBC reservation cannot be provided on the ground of religion."The appeasement politics of 'Congress Jinnah Party' has got a massive blow after the judgement was delivered," he said, noting that Congress govts have tried to give backward quota reservation to Muslims. TMC had done the same in Bengal and SP also advocated a similar quota, he added.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday sought responses from Centre, Delhi govt and Delhi Police on a PIL by NGO ‘Network of Women in Media’ seeking an independent probe, headed by a retired woman judge, into alleged incidents of sexual harassment of women journalists when they were covering the Oct 10 protests.Senior advocate Indira Jaising also mentioned about a woman journalist who was allegedly molested by a senior police officer, who in turn lodged an FIR under SC-ST Act against her for abusing him on caste lines. Such harassment of woman journalists, who form a class by themselves and must be protected while discharging their professional duties, must stop, she said.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta rebutted the charges and said the video purportedly depicting the police officer molesting the woman journalist is an AI-generated clip and that police would respond to the petition after completing investigation into the incident. But a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi directed that the journalist would not be arrested till further orders on the basis of the FIR.Jaising opposed and asked how police, which is accused of molesting a woman journalist, would investigate its officer. It must be handed over to an independent inquiry panel headed by a retired woman judge and comprising a retired woman IPS officer and eminent women representatives from civil society and NGOs.She said she is suggesting names for the composition of the panel from which the court can choose.When the bench allowed Jaising to give names of woman journalists who were allegedly sexually harassed during the protests and names for constituting the proposed panel in two separate sealed covers, Mehta said he opposed Jaising suggesting names for the panel. He said the court may take a call after police file their response to the petition.
Article Summary: Supreme Court seeks responses from Centre, Delhi govt and Delhi Police on a PIL by NGO ‘Network of Women in Media’ seeking an independent probe into alleged incidents of sexual harassment of women journalists when they were covering the Oct 10 protests. Senior advocate Indira Jaising also mentioned about a woman journalist who was allegedly molested by a senior police officer.

SRINAGAR: A crucial meeting on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Ladakhi representatives in Leh on Wednesday ended inconclusively, with both sides agreeing to hold talks again on Oct 22 in New Delhi.“The MHA team gave a presentation of its draft proposal and we submitted our draft. We found considerable gaps between the two. However, we have stressed that further discussions should take place soon,” Chering Dorjay Lakrook, co-chairman of Leh Apex Body (LAB), said Thursday.LAB member Sonam Wangchuk, who also attended the meeting, said the MHA would share a revised draft proposal with Ladakhi leaders on Friday morning as there was a huge gap between the drafts.“We will not say the meeting was a failure. It is a continuation process but it was not satisfactory. We are waiting for the revised draft and hope it will reflect some changes. The difference between the two proposals was like the difference between earth and sky. Instead of moving forward from the previous meeting, we have moved backwards,” Wangchuk said.Lakrook pointed out that LAB remained firm on its key demands including safeguards under Article 371 and a Union territory with a legislature.The last such meeting was held on Sept 9 in New Delhi. LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), the two Ladakh organisations negotiating with the Centre on autnomy, were part of the talks. Ladakh chief secretary of Ladakh Ashish Kundra had then spoken of “a sui generis model under Article 371 which does not exist anywhere in the country”.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the Centre since 2023 but the process stalled briefly after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.Earlier on Thursday, LAB condemned Beijing’s remarks on Ladakh, saying the region has never been part of China in recorded history but an integral part of India.
Article Summary: A crucial meeting on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Ladakhi representatives in Leh on Wednesday ended inconclusively. Both sides agreed to hold talks again on Oct 22 in New Delhi. LAB remained firm on its key demands including safeguards under Article 371 and a Union territory with a legislature.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said Thursday that development of Ladakh is a top priority for Centre, emphasising that special attention is being given to the youth of the UT to ensure that they get quality education and gain opportunities to learn new technologies, obviating the need for them to move to other cities.Virtually inaugurating five development projects covering airport infrastructure and strategic road connectivity in Ladakh worth around 3,350 crore, Modi said govt aims to develop modern infrastructure in the region while taking full care of the local environment.Prioritising the educational empowerment of the younger generation so they do not have to migrate to other cities, PM highlighted the construction of a major centre of excellence in Leh alongside advancing proposals for satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu."Our special focus is on the new generation of Ladakh. The youth of Ladakh will now be able to get better opportunities for higher education, research, and new skills right in their own region," he said."Together, we will take Ladakh to new heights of development," he said.Modi said several important development projects were inaugurated on Thursday, which will make travel easier for many people in Ladakh, improve electricity facilities in some areas, increase water availability in others, and strengthen the preservation of its ancient heritage.The projects include a new passenger terminal at the Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh, built for ₹640 crore.It incorporates geothermal energy to enhance energy efficiency and reduce its carbon footprint, reflecting the importance of sustainable infrastructure in Ladakh's ecologically sensitive environment.Modi also dedicated to the nation the 298-km-long Nimmu-Padum-Darcha Road, constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO), a 9 MW Hanu small hydroelectric project and the 66 kV double-circuit Dah-Hanu-Khaltsi transmission line. Besides, PM also inaugurated India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park at Sindhu Ghat in Leh and 40 water bodies developed across 40 villages under Project Him Sarovar.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi said development of Ladakh is a top priority for Centre. He emphasised that special attention is being given to the youth of the UT. Modi said govt aims to develop modern infrastructure in the region while taking full care of the local environment.
