JAMMU: In separate orders in two terror-related cases, a special NIA court in Jammu has declared a Rajouri native allegedly living in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir a “proclaimed offender” for repeatedly failing to appear before the court, while directing that forensic data extracted from a cellphone recovered at an encounter site be kept confidential and treated as “protected material”.Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the orders in separate proceedings on Wednesday.In the first case, the court declared Mushtaq Ahmed Mir, a native of Thanamang village in Rajouri’s Darhal tehsil, a proclaimed offender under BNSS Section 84. According to a report submitted by Darhal SHO, Mir allegedly crossed the Line of Control in 1995-96, joined terrorism and subsequently took shelter in PoK. A non-bailable warrant issued against him remained unexecuted.The court had issued a proclamation on July 20, 2026, directing Mir to appear. Despite publication in national and local English-language newspapers on Aug 13, he neither appeared nor surrendered. Observing that Mir was allegedly evading the legal process and that his arrest was not imminent, the court ordered that its proclamation order be sent to Govt Ranbir Press, Jammu, for publication in the Official Gazette.In another terror-related case, NIA told the court that Maneer Ahmed, arrested on April 15, 2026, was allegedly involved in harbouring terrorists and providing logistical support, including a cellphone, to ultras linked to an attack. During the investigation, a cellphone was recovered from an encounter site. Central Forensic Science Laboratory, Chandigarh, extracted its data.After examining NIA’s application and the relevant legal provisions, including Section 17 of NIA Act and Section 44 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, Justice Sagar ordered that the identified exhibit in the chargesheet be treated as protected material. The court clerk was directed not to disclose its contents during the trial and to preserve it in a sealed cover at a secure location within the court premises.
Article Summary: Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the orders in separate proceedings on Wednesday. In the first case, the court declared Mushtaq Ahmed Mir, a native of Thanamang village in Rajouri’s Darhal tehsil, a proclaimed offender under BNSS Section 84. In another terror-related case, NIA told the court that Maneer Ahmed was allegedly involved in harbouring terrorists.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday sought responses from EC, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by INDIA bloc functionaries led by Rahul Gandhi alleging irregularities in SIR, arbitrary deletion of voters, undemocratic functioning of the poll panel and flaws in EVM use, even as it slammed the suggestion that the court could be browbeaten by deploying crowds.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was issuing notices on the petition and would await the responses. NEW DELHI: The high-level committee studying causes and impact of "unnatural" demographic shifts in parts of the country has sought individual citizens' inputs on major demographic changes they have observed or studied over the past 15 years in the geographical areas they are familiar with.These geographical areas may be villages, towns, cities, districts, states/UTs, regions across India.In a questionnaire uploaded by the high-level committee on its dedicated portal, individual responders can provide causes of demographic changes, as perceived by them, besides detailing their likely effect on employment, education, healthcare, housing, infrastructure services, environment, social harmony and local economy. They have been further told to specify the challenges arising due to demographic changes. Individuals can also submit five recommendations to address these challenges.Wherever feasible, the committee requests, individuals must substantiate their responses with supporting material such as research reports, survey findings, case studies, photographs, audio-visual documentation, maps, official records, court records, media reports, publications or other relevant evidence.Respondents can attach documents with their responses.The portal - inaugurated Wednesday by committee chairperson Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar (Retd) - also puts out different sets of questionnaires for different stakeholders, including those in central ministries and departments, state govts, UT administration, NGOs, civil society, international organisations, think tanks, public servants and students.The stakeholders can, through the portal, give inputs/data/information on any abnormal settlement pattern cause that may have altered the demographic character of a region. "These inputs will help the committee to analyse and identify causes of demographic changes and to recommend a well-organised and permanent operational system for the legal, fair and time-bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants residing in the country," the committee said Wednesday.
Article Summary: The high-level committee is studying causes and impact of "unnatural" demographic shifts in parts of the country. It has sought individual citizens' inputs on major demographic changes they have observed or studied over the past 15 years. These geographical areas may be villages, towns, cities, districts, states/UTs, regions.

Article Title: Special summary revision of poll roll in 17 states
Article Text:
Only for voter list updation; paused post-2024

NEW DELHI: Election Commission Thursday ordered special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states/Union territories (UT) — including the five states due for assembly elections early next year — with reference to Jan 1, 2027 as the qualifying date.This is the first SSR exercise — which, unlike special intensive revision (SIR) that prepares electoral roll de novo, is a mere updation of the roll with no house-to-house visits by booth-level officers (BLOs) — to be undertaken after it was paused post-2024, on account of SIR that started with Bihar in June 2025 and has since covered 31 states/UTs in back-to-back phases. The third phase of SIR, covering 19 states/UTs, is still underway, with only a few states completed.As per the SSR schedule announced for 17 states/UTs — Assam, Andaman & Nicobar, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, MP, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, UP, Uttarakhand and West Bengal — rationalisation of polling stations will be completed by Nov 2.Draft rolls shall be published on Nov 12, followed by the claims and objections window from Nov 12 to Dec 11 and their disposal by Dec 28.Final rolls for the 17 states/UTs will be published on Jan 4, 2027.EC added that the schedule for the 19 states/UTs covered in Phase 3 as well as Himachal, J&K and Ladakh, where SIR has not yet been ordered, shall be announced later.The non-conduct of SSR after Jan 2024, barring Assam where it was completed ahead of polls earlier this year, was purportedly one of the points of alleged disagreements between ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, on the one hand, and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, on the other.
Article Summary: EC orders special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states/Union territories. This is the first SSR exercise to be undertaken after it was paused post-2024. The third phase of SIR covering 19 states/UTs is still underway, with only a few states completed.
